requirements.requirement: Pin a fresh baseline, source hashes, and individually authorized scope; keep MW separate from P04/P12.
A separate detail endpoint returns actual permitted content and a consistent current revision; the metadata endpoint is not automatically expanded.
Browse/history use bounded pagination, scope-bound cursors, reauthorization, and CURSOR_EXPIRED when the permitted snapshot changes.
Record exact source links for each new revision; mark historical provenance legacy_unattributed when its revision-level basis cannot be established.
Context returns sections and rendered_context from the same data, without substituting an explanation for missing source content.
The UTF-8 limit covers the complete rendered context; accept a strict token_budget only with a qualified counter.
Every read surface, MCP, and export checks content/disclosure permissions before returning text or diagnostic metadata.
Correction/import reuse the current authority and one caller-owned unit of work for data, audit, outbox, and receipt.
An exact committed replay is authorized under current permissions, returns the same IDs, and does not repeat the mutation.
Different intentions under one key conflict; random response IDs do not participate in semantic equality.
Correction requires expected content/state revisions; restore creates a new revision and cannot downgrade the obligations of historical content.
Legacy adapters cannot bypass the shared writer or change historical receipt semantics without an explicit compatibility policy.
Console uses the HTTP SDK and existing design system, without direct database access.
The editor retains drafts on conflict/unknown outcome, retries an unknown POST with the same key, and never automatically overwrites.
Workspace switching discards late responses from the previous scope and clears content caches/drafts.
Imported content is not executed as HTML/scripts; verify keyboard, focus, and error states in a real browser.
Source identity is a scoped external UUID; path and content hash do not replace identity.
SourceRevision is immutable; source content remains distinct from effective memory and human corrections.
Preview binds durably stored exact bytes and base versions; it does not authorize changed input.
Staging/export use the ordinary material lifecycle, not plaintext in a new temporary directory or table.
The scanner reads only an explicit root, follows no symlink/junction/reparse point, and rejects traversal/absolute paths.
Enforce 64 KiB per file, 100 items, and 8 MiB per batch using decoded UTF-8 bytes; reject duplicate JSON keys and excessive depth.
Import does not invoke an LLM by default and creates a source-excerpt observation, not a confirmed fact.
Apply uses a registered existing OutboxHandler with an atomic item receipt; 202 does not mean successful or indexed.
Worker replay after item commit but before acknowledgement creates no additional revision, audit record, or outbox entry.
Reauthorize the original actor during Apply; worker service identity cannot bypass revoked permission.
An unchanged source creates no canonical revision; a rename with established identity changes its locator, not memory content.
B/I/M comparison preserves human edits; conflicts are never resolved by silent latest-wins or automatic LLM merging.
Accept/keep/merge require all preconditions and an atomic resolution, binding, and memory receipt.
Missing is an observation, not Delete; incomplete scans cannot mark uninspected files missing.
A collection has at most one active Apply; verify mutation guards and lock ordering with actual races.
Cancellation preserves committed items and stops uncommitted ones; expiry/cleanup cannot treat a timeout as proof of writer death.
JSON export contains only the permitted bounded selection, not secrets, keys, grants, vectors, or qualification verdicts.
Download reauthorizes the complete pinned selection; revocation/purge blocks an old result and initiates lawful erasure.
Portable import validates version, shape, limits, and intra-package references before canonical Apply and allocates new local IDs.
Foreign actor, time, trust, and labels are annotations, not local authority; selected history is not full installation history.
Portable source links close in a second idempotent pass of the same handler; partial progress is reported explicitly.
Markdown export is a human-readable representation, not a guaranteed round-trip restoration of all metadata.
Forward migrations and exact grants pass clean-install, upgrade, and refusal tests; existing migrations are never edited.
Acceptance uses the actual binary, worker, HTTP, and Console; raw seeding cannot replace missing production producers.
Code, schema, SDK, and manual agree; the proposed OpenAPI subset does not replace the entire served OpenAPI.
Test doctests separately from --all-targets; UI scripts and browser dependencies remain proposed until implemented.
Readiness/index states follow existing generation/material authorities; no raw-provider fallback is allowed.
Keep raw content, source names, and host paths out of logs, metrics, and denial details; provide separately authorized scoped diagnostics.
Public claims identify build, environment, version, and limitations; source inspection is not runtime evidence.

acceptance_cases.name: Baseline reconciliation
acceptance_cases.given: Main differs from the pinned SHA or a module/migration with the proposed name already exists
acceptance_cases.then: Do not write; update baseline, gaps, and exact scope through an explicit reviewed diff
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Continue under the old scope

acceptance_cases.name: Detail hydration
acceptance_cases.given: Memory r2 belongs to W1 and its source event is permitted; W2 knows the same UUID
acceptance_cases.then: W1 receives exact r2 content/state; W2 receives a uniform 404 without text or source IDs
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Reveal W1 source metadata in a denial

acceptance_cases.name: Browse pagination
acceptance_cases.given: Three records share created_at, page size is 2, and a correction occurs between pages 1 and 2
acceptance_cases.then: Use the ID tie-breaker; after mutation return CURSOR_EXPIRED
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Silently omit or repeat records

acceptance_cases.name: History authorization
acceptance_cases.given: Revision r1 is denied and r2 permitted; request history and the direct r1 URL
acceptance_cases.then: Withhold r1 content and its protected source while keeping r2 available
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Authorize the entire history using only the r2 label

acceptance_cases.name: Exact provenance
acceptance_cases.given: Legacy memory_sources has no revision link; a new correction has an exact link
acceptance_cases.then: Mark old associations legacy_unattributed and new ones exact; timestamps create no inferred links
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Attach a legacy source to the nearest revision by timestamp

acceptance_cases.name: Actual context content
acceptance_cases.given: A candidate has empty content and a nonempty technical explanation
acceptance_cases.then: Explicitly omit it; do not present the explanation as source knowledge
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Render the explanation as a fact

acceptance_cases.name: UTF-8 budget
acceptance_cases.given: Russian/emoji text and long citations approach the byte cap
acceptance_cases.then: The final rendered_context fits max_utf8_bytes, including separators
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Count only source content before adding citations

acceptance_cases.name: Qualified tokenizer
acceptance_cases.given: A token_budget is supplied without a tokenizer or with an unknown tokenizer
acceptance_cases.then: Reject structurally or return TOKEN_COUNTER_UNAVAILABLE; never claim enforced=true falsely
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Use ceil(bytes / 4) as an exact token count

acceptance_cases.name: Disclosure boundary
acceptance_cases.given: An otherwise permitted ID selection includes a source denied by label/destination policy
acceptance_cases.then: No forbidden text, snippet, or title appears in context, detail, source views, or errors
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Filter only after disclosing content to the reranker

acceptance_cases.name: Atomic rollback
acceptance_cases.given: Inject a fault after revision INSERT but before audit/outbox/receipt
acceptance_cases.then: Roll back all canonical changes and retain the old active head and epoch
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Commit memory without its outbox entry

acceptance_cases.name: Lost-response replay
acceptance_cases.given: A correction commits, the HTTP response is lost, and the same body/key is retried
acceptance_cases.then: Return the original receipt with one revision, audit record, and outbox entry
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Check stale CAS before replay and return a false conflict

acceptance_cases.name: Same-key race
acceptance_cases.given: Two independent connections submit the same key/body with different generated result UUIDs
acceptance_cases.then: One winner; the other request receives the same receipt without duplicates
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Compare a random audit UUID and spuriously conflict

acceptance_cases.name: Changed intent
acceptance_cases.given: Two bodies use one key but differ in target, content, or reason
acceptance_cases.then: Return 409 without a second mutation
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Treat key equality alone as semantic request equality

acceptance_cases.name: Concurrent editors
acceptance_cases.given: A and B read r3/state4; A commits and B submits the old basis
acceptance_cases.then: B receives a conflict while A's content remains
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Silent last-write-wins

acceptance_cases.name: Restore as a new revision
acceptance_cases.given: Active r4 and permitted historical r1 exist; restore r1 using r4 as the expected basis
acceptance_cases.then: Create r5 with r1 content, preserve r2–r4, and do not lower the label
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Move the active pointer to r1 and destroy history

acceptance_cases.name: Legacy compatibility
acceptance_cases.given: Replay legacy create/revise requests and apply a new correction to the same memory
acceptance_cases.then: Preserve the old wire shape and numeric If-Match through the shared writer
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Leave a non-atomic bypass in the legacy route

acceptance_cases.name: SDK error handling
acceptance_cases.given: The server returns 503 unavailable rather than an empty array
acceptance_cases.then: Show unavailable and retain the standard request_id for diagnostics
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Display an empty library instead of the error

acceptance_cases.name: Draft with unknown outcome
acceptance_cases.given: POST times out after sending and the user selects check/retry
acceptance_cases.then: Preserve the draft and reuse the same body/key rather than creating a new save
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Automatically allocate another UUID key

acceptance_cases.name: Workspace switching
acceptance_cases.given: A W1 request is slow and the user switches to W2
acceptance_cases.then: Discard the late W1 response and clear W1 caches/drafts
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Display W1 content inside W2

acceptance_cases.name: Hostile rendering
acceptance_cases.given: Markdown includes script/img/javascript URLs and a third-party tracking pixel
acceptance_cases.then: The text view executes nothing and loads no remote resource
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Pass imported content to dangerouslySetInnerHTML

acceptance_cases.name: Keyboard accessibility
acceptance_cases.given: Open editor, restore, and conflict resolution using only a keyboard
acceptance_cases.then: Expose names, focus, errors, and status accessibly; restore focus after closing dialogs
acceptance_cases.counterexample: An unexplained inaccessible control or lost focus

acceptance_cases.name: Source identity
acceptance_cases.given: Two source UUIDs contain identical bytes but identify different sources
acceptance_cases.then: Keep distinct source identities; byte deduplication does not merge provenance or ACLs
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Use one source identity per content hash

acceptance_cases.name: Source revision immutability
acceptance_cases.given: Raw runtime-role SQL attempts to replace the r1 source payload
acceptance_cases.then: Refuse through the asserted constraint/privilege while allowing lawful r2 creation
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Update historical bytes in place

acceptance_cases.name: Pinned preview bytes
acceptance_cases.given: A local file changes after preview; Apply uses the same preview ID
acceptance_cases.then: Apply pinned bytes or require a new preview, never substitute changed bytes
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Read the live file again during Apply

acceptance_cases.name: Staging process death
acceptance_cases.given: A process dies before ContentPrepared and, in a separate case, after ContentPrepared
acceptance_cases.then: Before preparation require needs_upload and lawful retirement; after preparation resume exact stored ciphertext
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Fabricate a receipt or use plaintext fallback

acceptance_cases.name: Scanner root confinement
acceptance_cases.given: Inputs include traversal, absolute paths, symlinks, junctions, case collisions, and a state file inside the root
acceptance_cases.then: Refuse or explicitly skip before upload; unsupported modes fail closed
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Rely only on startsWith(root) without handle checks

acceptance_cases.name: Input limits
acceptance_cases.given: Try 40,000 Cyrillic ya characters, 101 files, duplicate JSON keys, and depth 33
acceptance_cases.then: Reject byte/count/duplicate/depth violations before applying any item
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Truncate input and declare success

acceptance_cases.name: Source excerpt is not authority
acceptance_cases.given: A document says the agent is permitted administrator access
acceptance_cases.then: Store an Observation/source excerpt without changing grants or configuration
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Execute the embedded instruction

acceptance_cases.name: Production handler wiring
acceptance_cases.given: Create preview and Apply through HTTP, then run the actual worker --once
acceptance_cases.then: The registered topic produces a durable item receipt; track indexing separately
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Call only the service directly instead of using the worker

acceptance_cases.name: Crash before acknowledgement
acceptance_cases.given: The worker dies after the item transaction commits but before outbox acknowledgement
acceptance_cases.then: Replay converges on the original receipt and a single revision
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Create another source revision during replay

acceptance_cases.name: Revoked initiating actor
acceptance_cases.given: Revoke the creator's capability between preview and Apply
acceptance_cases.then: Record blocked_policy without content in the error; the worker cannot substitute an administrator
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Write with the worker's broader authority

acceptance_cases.name: Unchanged source and rename
acceptance_cases.given: Rescan the same external_id/content and then explicitly change only the locator
acceptance_cases.then: The first creates no revision; the second records a locator event without duplicating memory
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Create new memory on every scan

acceptance_cases.name: Source/editor conflict
acceptance_cases.given: Import B, edit memory into M, then receive upstream I different from B
acceptance_cases.then: Keep M current and preserve an open conflict with exact B/I/M references
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Overwrite M under the name of synchronization

acceptance_cases.name: Three explicit resolutions
acceptance_cases.given: Use separate fixtures for accept_source, keep_manual, and merge
acceptance_cases.then: Apply I and clear override, preserve M with override, or create a merged revision; record audit and receipt in every branch
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Modify incoming I while keeping manual content

acceptance_cases.name: Stale conflict basis
acceptance_cases.given: M changes again after the conflict was inspected
acceptance_cases.then: Resolve returns 409 without losing the new manual revision; retrieve fresh basis data
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Resolve against current content the user never inspected

acceptance_cases.name: Partial scan versus Missing
acceptance_cases.given: A file is omitted from a partial scan and separately from a complete manifest
acceptance_cases.then: Partial asserts no Missing; complete records Missing without Delete
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Delete memory because a file disappeared

acceptance_cases.name: Competing batches
acceptance_cases.given: Two Apply requests target one collection while an editor changes a memory between items
acceptance_cases.then: Only one batch is active; per-item CAS observes the edit and produces a conflict where necessary
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Run two independent overwrite queues

acceptance_cases.name: Cancellation race
acceptance_cases.given: Item A commits and cancellation wins before item B commits
acceptance_cases.then: Preserve A, do not apply B, and report the partial/cancelled outcome explicitly
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Compensate A as though its committed change never happened

acceptance_cases.name: Expiry race
acceptance_cases.given: Preview expiry races Apply
acceptance_cases.then: Exactly one lawful winner under collection/operation locks; cleanup cannot erase a live applied payload
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Erase a payload already owned by an applied source

acceptance_cases.name: Export scope
acceptance_cases.given: Select two memories while a denied third exists but is not selected
acceptance_cases.then: Include only the two selected memories and permitted sources, without tokens, grants, or vectors
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Serialize an entire internal domain object

acceptance_cases.name: Revocation before download
acceptance_cases.given: Export is ready, then access to one pinned revision is revoked
acceptance_cases.then: Block the entire download with 403/blocked, retire the result, and prevent old-URL bypass
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Return cached JSON after the ACL changes

acceptance_cases.name: Malformed portable input
acceptance_cases.given: Supply a future version, unknown authority fields, or dangling links
acceptance_cases.then: Refuse before canonical Apply; distinguish schema from semantic rejection
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Ignore foreign permissions and silently apply part of the package without reporting it

acceptance_cases.name: Portable replay
acceptance_cases.given: Different workers deliver the same operation twice
acceptance_cases.then: Reuse the same local mappings with unchanged content/history/link counts
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Allocate new local IDs on replay

acceptance_cases.name: Foreign trust boundaries
acceptance_cases.given: Imported annotations claim an administrator actor, a past time, and public classification
acceptance_cases.then: Use the actual importer and local recording time; retain origin annotations and reevaluate target policy
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Grant local administrator authority from package content

acceptance_cases.name: Restart during linking
acceptance_cases.given: Memories/sources commit and the worker dies before the linking pass
acceptance_cases.then: The same topic resumes mappings and links; keep provenance partial until closure
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Introduce an unregistered topic that remains pending forever

acceptance_cases.name: Markdown export
acceptance_cases.given: Content contains delimiters, headings, and links
acceptance_cases.then: Produce a readable escaped document with completeness limitations and no full-round-trip claim
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Turn Markdown metadata into executable code

acceptance_cases.name: Populated-baseline upgrade
acceptance_cases.given: A baseline database contains legacy memories/sources; apply candidate migrations
acceptance_cases.then: Preserve history and metadata, do not fabricate provenance, and retain restricted-role operation
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Test only a fresh empty database

acceptance_cases.name: Direct SQL denial
acceptance_cases.given: The runtime role directly writes every new guarded table
acceptance_cases.then: Assert the intended privilege/constraint refusal while lawful commands pass
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Treat a superuser fixture as runtime-role proof

acceptance_cases.name: Golden end-to-end workflow
acceptance_cases.given: Upload → find → edit → sync conflict → resolve → export → new target
acceptance_cases.then: Use ordinary binaries, worker, and browser; administrative seeding is limited to installation bootstrap
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Insert the expected outcome directly in the fixture

acceptance_cases.name: Contract parity
acceptance_cases.given: Compare served OpenAPI, typed client, and actual JSON for every new route
acceptance_cases.then: Fields/statuses agree and the legacy metadata contract is unchanged
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Check only the static schemas/openapi-v1.json file

acceptance_cases.name: Doctest execution
acceptance_cases.given: A type has a compile_fail doctest and CI runs all-targets separately
acceptance_cases.then: A separate --doc invocation actually executes and the named scripts exist
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Count all-targets as doctest execution

acceptance_cases.name: Search readiness
acceptance_cases.given: A canonical source is applied while its generation is not ready
acceptance_cases.then: Show pending/blocked and a typed retrieval error
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Equate imported with search-ready

acceptance_cases.name: Sensitive log exclusion
acceptance_cases.given: Submit an invalid document containing a secret and request denied history
acceptance_cases.then: Logs contain safe IDs/codes, not content, absolute paths, or keys
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Print request bodies or SQL bind values

acceptance_cases.name: Release claim boundary
acceptance_cases.given: Only unit tests/typechecking ran, without PostgreSQL/browser execution
acceptance_cases.then: Block a release claim and record not-run checks; documentation checks are not product qualification
acceptance_cases.counterexample: Treat green syntax checks as complete implementation
